entries.reason: Renamed Rust crates still contain ADR-020-governed PQUEUE_* configuration aliases, persisted pqueue_* identifiers, RESP pqueue tokens, and historical bead references; the dedicated Cargo/Rust namespace check rejects old package, import, path, and Rust-owned binary coordinates independently.
entries.owner_surface: Rust runtime compatibility, persistence/wire identifiers, and audit references
entries.removal_condition: Remove after the configuration, protocol, and persisted-data owners retire the remaining pqueue and PQUEUE compatibility identifiers and historical references no longer require scanning.

entries.reason: ADR-020 classifies the existing Helm chart, rendered workload names, chart package name, and runtime environment prefix as temporary compatibility aliases.
entries.owner_surface: Helm chart and Kubernetes deployment manifests
entries.removal_condition: Remove after charts/fireweed-queue is authoritative and old pqueue chart/rendered coordinates are either migrated or separately retained by an operator compatibility ADR.

entries.reason: ADR-020 identifies CI, release, checkout paths, repository URLs, and downstream workflow consumers as migration surfaces that must keep old coordinates during the dual-name period.
entries.owner_surface: GitHub Actions CI and release automation
entries.removal_condition: Remove when workflows check out fireweed-queue, publish Fireweed artifacts, and no CI job depends on pqueue compatibility coordinates.

entries.reason: ADR-020 distinguishes operator-facing examples from retained on-disk and runtime wire identifiers such as /var/lib/pqueue and PQUEUE_* compatibility variables.
entries.removal_condition: Remove after public deployment examples use Fireweed coordinates and any retained pqueue storage or wire identifiers are covered by a separate data-migration ADR.

entries.reason: The generated operator console remains tied to the current pqueue service and chart examples until the Fireweed public examples are rendered.
entries.removal_condition: Remove when generated operator examples are rebuilt with Fireweed public naming.

entries.reason: ADR-020 preserves historical release notes, evidence ledgers, benchmark commands, and audit artifacts without rewriting published history.
entries.owner_surface: Release evidence, performance evidence, and historical release notes
entries.removal_condition: Remove only if a later evidence-retention decision supersedes the no-history-rewrite policy for these tracked artifacts.

entries.reason: ADR-020 keeps historical naming analysis, bead IDs, accepted decisions, and migration inventory visible for auditability.
entries.owner_surface: HELIX governance documents and ADR-020 migration inventory
entries.removal_condition: Remove only when ADR-020 is replaced by a new governance artifact that explicitly rewrites this tracked documentation policy.

entries.reason: ADR-020 classifies current public docs, container image names, local service names, and runtime coordinates as temporary compatibility surfaces.
entries.owner_surface: Repository root public docs and runtime packaging
entries.removal_condition: Remove when root docs and runtime packaging advertise Fireweed coordinates and any old local names are covered by a dedicated compatibility note.

entries.reason: ADR-020 lists release, perf, CI, and identity-guardrail scripts as consumers that must recognize old names during the migration window.
entries.owner_surface: CI, release, performance, and development scripts
entries.removal_condition: Remove when operational scripts invoke Fireweed coordinates only and no longer need old pqueue compatibility variables or binary names.

entries.reason: The ADR-020 residue gate and its tests must name each old identity class so they can reject newly introduced unapproved occurrences.
entries.removal_condition: Remove when the guardrail no longer tests old pqueue, PQUEUE, Queueyard, or 7thsense-pqueue residues because those classes have fully retired.
